pages.title: Child and Adolescent Development (I-A-2)
pages.description:
© 2017 Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education. Reproduced for non-commercial educational purposes with attribution under the permission in the official Guidebook. Commercial embedding and translation permission are not established. Digital transcription for teacher reflection. You may leave any field blank. No score is calculated. Use de-identified evidence; do not enter student names or identifying case details. Narrative fields have a project technical limit of 2000 characters. This is not a signed evaluation form. Standard I: Curriculum, Planning, and Assessment
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Demonstrates knowledge of the developmental levels of students in the classroom and the different ways these students learn by providing differentiated learning experiences that enable all students to progress toward meeting intended outcomes.
• Designs the developmentally appropriate learning environment to support all students’ learning by facilitating various learning activities, integrating multiple opportunities for student action and expression, and collaboration with peers.

pages.title: Variety of Assessment Methods (I-B-1)
pages.description:
Standard I: Curriculum, Planning, and Assessment
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Designs and administers a variety of informal and formal methods and assessments, including common interim assessments, to measure each student’s learning, growth, and progress toward achieving state/local standards.
• Conducts frequent checks for student understanding and uses data to drive instruction
• Provides multiple and varied options for student communication and expression to demonstrate understanding and build fluency

pages.title: Adjustment to Practice (I-B-2)
pages.description:
Standard I: Curriculum, Planning, and Assessment
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Organizes and analyzes results from a variety of assessments to determine progress toward intended outcomes and uses these findings to adjust practice and identify and/or implement appropriate differentiated interventions and enhancements for students.
• Ensures assessments are accessible such that all students’ knowledge can be demonstrated and accurately captured
• Provides frequent and varied feedback and positive reinforcement to student responses

pages.title: Meeting Diverse Needs (II-A-3)
pages.description:
Standard II: Teaching All Students
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Uses appropriate practices, including tiered instruction and scaffolds, to accommodate differences in learning styles, needs, interests, and levels of readiness, including those of students with disabilities and English learners.
• Identifies and removes curricular and/or instructional barriers to student learning
• Familiarizes themselves with student learning profiles (IEPs, 504s, WIDA report cards) and uses information to guide instruction
• Utilizes evidence based practices and district supports (UDL, PBIS, SEL, SEI, DCAP)

pages.title: Safe Learning Environment (II-B-1)
pages.description:
Standard II: Teaching All Students
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Uses rituals, routines, and appropriate responses that create and maintain a safe physical and intellectual environment.
• Promotes academic risk taking
• Utilizes preventative measures to minimize behaviors that interfere with learning.
• Fosters collaboration and community by creating an accepting and supportive classroom climate that is sensitive to individual learner profiles
• Creates a nonthreatening, positive, and academically rigorous atmosphere and integrated with other important initiatives

pages.title: Access to Knowledge (II-D-3)
pages.description:
Standard II: Teaching All Students
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Consistently adapts instruction, materials, and assessments to make challenging material accessible to all students, including English learners and students with disabilities.
• Presents curriculum content through multiple means and provides scaffolds and supports for metacognitive processing

pages.title: Two Way Communication (III-C-1)
pages.description:
Standard III: Family and Community Engagement
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Regularly uses two-way communication with families about student performance and learning and responds promptly and carefully to communications from families.
• Establishes a welcoming and family friendly classroom
• Utilizes multiple means of communication to reach all families
• Is sensitive to cultural and other demographic considerations when communicating with families

pages.title: Reflective Practice (IV-A-1)
pages.description:
Standard IV: Professional Culture
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Regularly reflects on the effectiveness of lessons, units, and interactions with students, both individually and with colleagues, and uses insights gained to improve practice and student learning.
• Utilizes a variety of approaches to gather information, analyze data, examine issues, set meaningful goals, and develop new approaches in order to improve inclusive practices
• Regularly assesses all student performance to determine effectiveness of instructional practice

pages.title: Shared Responsibility (IV-E-1)
pages.description:
Standard IV: Professional Culture
Proficient Descriptor and Inclusive Practice Examples
Within and beyond the classroom, consistently reinforces school-wide behavior and learning expectations for all students, and contributes to their learning by sharing responsibility for meeting their needs.
• Collaborates with others to ensure alignment of instructional plans and academic expectations
• Collaborates with others to align practices, routines, and vocabulary for behavior
• Shares and discusses student data and problem solves collaboratively
